messages:
incbot: PAGER — GEO-DNS: elevated resolver probe failures from Cloudflare edge -> multiple NXDOMAINs observed for us-east-1 prefixes. Error rate 34% (last 5m). Auto-fallback not triggered due to threshold config. Paging oncall.

alex (oncall): acked. investigating now. digging into probe logs + recent config rolls. giving ETA 10m. @jordan can you take netops lead? :wave:

jordan (netops): on it. seeing a spike of SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN from a subset of CF resolvers, roughly IPs matching cf-us-east datacenter pool. looks like query amplification/backpressure on their side.

alice (sre): adding some logs — sample dig output from our probe: ```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> @1.1.1.1 customer.example.com A +short
server: 1.1.1.1#53(1.1.1.1)
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 53124
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0
```

alex (oncall): confirmed. customer-facing requests show elevated 502/504s for a small % of traffic routed to us-east via geo mapping. Not widespread but steady. Maria FYI.

maria (product): thx. which customers are impacted? any paying customers with traffic spikes?

alice (sre): quick impact breakdown: ~2.1% of global requests saw DNS resolution failures mapping to us-east; top 3 tenants by traffic: tenant-a, tenant-c, tenant-x. No sign of data plane failure once resolved; errors are DNS-only.

jordan (netops): proposed mitigations:
1) throttle outgoing probe rate to CF for 60s (circuit-breaker)
2) temporarily pin geo answers for us-east to Route53 fallback pool (ttl 30s)
3) raise probe threshold to trigger auto-fallback sooner if problem persists
I can execute 1+2 now. prefer low-risk: 1 then 2 if improvement < 50%.

alex (oncall): do it. document commands you run here.

jordan (netops): running probe throttle: ```
/ops/control geodns --scope probes --region us-east --action throttle --rate 10/s --duration 60
```

eng-deploy-bot: action accepted. geodns-probe-throttle(us-east) queued -> applied to 6 workers.

jordan (netops): throttle applied. watching metrics.

(2m pass)

alice (sre): DNS error rate dropped from 34% -> 18% after throttle. still above baseline. applying step 2: pin to Route53 fallback for us-east for 15m. command: ```
/ops/control geodns --region us-east --failover-provider route53 --mode pin --ttl 30 --duration 900
```

eng-deploy-bot: failover-rule applied: geo us-east -> route53 (ttl 30) ; duration=900s.

(30s pass)

alex (oncall): visible improvement in customer traffic. resolved DNS errors now ~3.5%. still slightly elevated but within acceptable range. keeping pinned for full 15m then reassess.

maria (product): can we notify affected tenants? Taylor pls coordinate with customer-ops for short note.

taylor (customer-ops): will send a brief: "We observed intermittent DNS resolution errors affecting requests to us-east; mitigation applied, service restored for most traffic. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up if we see regression." Drafting now.

jordan (netops): FYI we also added a temporary circuit-breaker to stop forwarding queries to the noisy CF resolver IP range. We'll remove once stable.

alex (oncall): good. next steps: 1) keep failover pinned 15m 2) increase probe sampling diversity (add additional upstream resolvers) 3) run root-cause follow-up with CF support if errors reappear. I'll hand off to night oncall in 45m if stable.

(10m later)

alice (sre): metrics steady. DNS error ~1.2% now. no new customer escalations.

alex (oncall): preparing incident summary for postmortem and handoff. main action items logged.

alex (oncall): HANDOFF -> @sre-night (oncall) for monitoring until 0600 UTC. If error rate >5% in next hour, escalate to netops and product.

eng-deploy-bot: pinned rule expires in 600s. auto-notify on expiry.

alex (oncall): closing paging loop. thanks team :thumbsup: — will open follow-up ticket to review geodns thresholding and add probe backoff logic to prevent future noisy-prober amplification.

(incident metadata note)
alex (oncall): customer-impact: brief DNS-only failures for subset of tenants in us-east; no data-plane loss; estimated 2-3% of requests affected during peak; mitigation: probe throttle + failover to Route53; status: mitigated, monitoring.

jordan (netops): filing ticket with CF support (case #CF-98765) to trace internal resolver instability and request better egress policing.

alex (oncall): thanks all. leaving the thread for follow-up.
